chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The people are upon six divisions, which all return to three divisions: Faith, Disbelief, and Straying. And they are the People of the Two Promises, whom Allah has promised Paradise and Hell: The Believers and the Disbelievers; The Weak and the Hopeful for Allah's Command, either He punishes them or He repents for them; And those who confess their sins, who mixed a righteous deed with an evil one; And the People of Al-A'raf.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْوَعْدَيْن: People of the Two Promises (Paradise and Hell)

ai.seo_question: What are the six divisions of people according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates six distinct categories of humanity, which ultimately converge into three eschatological outcomes: Faith, Disbelief, and Straying. This classification highlights the 'People of the Heights' (Ahl al-A'raf) as a unique intermediate group, often interpreted in Shia scholarship as those whose good and bad deeds are balanced, awaiting Allah's final mercy or judgment. The hadith underscores the theological concept of 'Ahl al-Wa'dayn' (People of the Two Promises), linking the Believers and Disbelievers to their respective eternal destinations of Paradise and Hell.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Hamza Bin Al Tayyar who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The people are upon six divisions. All of these can be interpreted to be upon three divisions – the Emān, and the Kufr (disbelief), and the straying. And they are the Promised people whom Allahazwj has Promised the Paradise and the Fire – the Momineen, and the Unbelivers, and the weak ones, and the hopeful ones for the Command of Allahazwj, either Heazwj Punishes them or Heazwj Turns towards them (with Mercy), and the acknowledgers of their sins mixing the righteous deeds and the evil deeds, and the people of the Heights’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Ubayd from Yunus from Hammad from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“People are of six categories. All of them come from three groups: people of belief, disbelief and straying. All three are the people of two promises. Allah has promised paradise and fire. There are the believers, and the unbelievers. Besides, there are the weak ones who hope in the command of Allah whereby they may be punished or forgiven and there are those who have confessed to their sins and have mixed good deeds with bad deeds. Also there are the people of ‘A’raf. (Straying people are of four groups and with the other two: believing people and unbelievers total six groups).”
